about: Process plan for the Contour TPG322 triangle insert with a ground chipbreaker, on the shop's 10 x 24 manual surface grinder (grinder-1), on its own 10 x 24 fine-pole permanent magnetic chuck (from its CAD; Suburban's MCB-1024-FP is the chuck it stands for, moonshot/library/stations/sgrind.json; the 6 x 18 chuck on the cart, magchk, is a spare), then a quick check: the shop's own routing (Harig grinder, quick check), and the drawing's note 1, 'Grind chipbreaker on Harig'. The insert is bought ground to size, periphery, nose radii, 11 deg clearance and both faces, and only the chipbreaker is ground here. C2 carbide holds on the chuck at only about 5% of steel's grip, so it is blocked in with ground steel keepers set tight round it, which the magnet holds (your decision, 2026-11-06). A manual grinder's table, cross-feed and down-feed are cranked by hand, so each edge's grind is people's work at the handwheels, not a machine cycle; its video may show a few strokes with the rest cut, each cut declared (your decision, 2026-11-06). The down-feed handwheel is 1.4 m up on the column's right side, out of reach from the table's handwheel at the front, so each pass is two takes: the table rocked from the front, then the wheel fed down from the right side, the passes joined by declared cuts; the coolant is SB1029's optional flood coolant, its switch on the control box and its nozzle on the guard (your decision, 2026-11-06; moonshot/planning/takes.py grind_takes). Written by Claude from the drawing (a modelled lookalike, in inches) and the STEP model; every feature below is checked against the model by moonshot/planning/validate.py. Model frame: Z is thickness (the Z=0 face is the bottom, the Z=3.175 face the top), the triangle lies in XY with its inscribed circle centred on the origin, the first edge the one at X=+4.763 (outward +X), its noses' centres at (3.97, ±6.87) and the third nose's at (-7.94, 0). The chipbreaker is a ring round the three edges: a .010 land at the top, a groove .055 wide and .008 deep inside it (the floor at Z=2.972), then the raised plateau. A surface grinder's wheel grinds a straight slot along each edge, running out along its own arc at the stroke's ends, and must stop short of each nose or it notches the next edge: the STEP's ring round the noses, at full depth, is beyond it. So the stock compare exempts the three nose regions, as what a straight wheel leaves (like G1's round-tool exemptions), and holds each edge's floor to 0.1 mm where the wheel reaches it, from 3.1 to 13.4 mm along its 16.5 mm (your decisions, 2026-11-06: the noses exempt, then widened from 2.9 to 3.1 mm to take in the groove's three inner corners, the R0.127 rounds 1.78 mm in from both edges that neither slot's wheel reaches, which read 0.127 mm against the 0.1).

stock.size_in: .375 IC triangle x .125, 1/32 nose, 11 deg clearance
stock.from: a TPGN 322 C2 insert, bought ground to size with no chipbreaker [proposed: the drawing gives only the finished insert, and its routing's one operation is the chipbreaker on the grinder]

setups.title: Op 10: chipbreaker
setups.coolant: SB1029's optional flood coolant: its switch on the control box, its nozzle on the guard, aimed at the wheel's cut (your decision, 2026-11-06)

place.layout: a pinwheel: each keeper along one flank, from one of its corners out past the next, so none crosses another
place.back_keeper: along the chuck's back edge, flush with it (0-12.7 mm in), against the edge being ground, running left from the insert's back corner
place.front_left_keeper: along the insert's front-left flank from its back-left corner, running front-right, 12.7-52.0 mm in from the back edge
place.front_right_keeper: along the front-right flank from the insert's front corner, running back-right, its outer corner 6.0 mm past the back edge (its three other corners on the chuck hold it, 19 mm ahead of the spindle's housing at the work)

workholding.note: Blocked in on the chuck by three of the shop's grinding keepers (keepers-1): 1/8 x 1/2 in precision ground O-1 flat stock cut 1-1/2 in long, laid flat, 12.7 mm wide and 1/8 in high, set tight against the insert's three flanks in a pinwheel (your decision, 2026-11-06: ground steel keepers; the shop's 6 in parallels, laid round a triangle with a flank along the travel, reach 256 mm across the table, past the 254 mm chuck, and run over 120 mm behind the insert into the spindle housing's path). Flat they stand 1/8 in, the insert's own .125, so nothing stands above its top; each holds about 100 N. The insert's 11 deg flank faces a little downward, so a keeper's push on it lifts it by about 0.19 of any sideways push: a hard sideways knock (over about 6.5 N, against its 1.15 N pull and its weight) wedges it up over its keepers, which a pass's down-force prevents, and the hand only nudges it once they are set (moonshot/tests/test_grind_cell.py). Where it sits (the grinder's station, 2026-11-06): the first keeper lies along the chuck's back edge, flush with it, which squares it to the table's travel, and the edge being ground lies against it, the insert's 11 deg flank leaning away below its cutting edge so the keeper touches it at the top, 12.7 mm in from the chuck's back edge. Its groove runs 12.95-14.35 mm in from the back edge and the insert's top covers 12.7-26.2 mm. That keeps the work within the 38 mm of the back edge where the spindle's housing, which hangs 23 mm below the 6 in wheel's bottom from 38.7 mm behind its plane, stays behind the chuck, and inside the back 202 mm of its 254 that the cross travel reaches past the column. The wheel's side, at the land's .010 inside the edge, passes 0.25 mm clear of the back keeper on the first cross position and 0.76 mm on the second. For the next edge the coolant is switched off and the table run clear of the wheel, the magnet switched off, the insert turned 120 deg between the same keepers, which its symmetry fits, the next edge against the back keeper, and the magnet and the coolant switched on again. The land's .010 is held to .XXX's ±.005, which a keeper flush with the chuck's ground back edge meets

datum.z: the insert's top: the wheel touched down on it and the down-feed dial zeroed
datum.cross: the cutting edge: the wheel's outer side set .010 in inside it with the cross-feed, by the dial from the wheel's side touched on the edge

operations.what: Grind the first edge's chipbreaker: the coolant switched on, then .055 wide and .008 deep, .010 in from the edge, in two cross positions .020 in apart, each pass the table rocked about 3 mm along the edge's middle from the front and the wheel fed down .0005 in from the column's right side

region.note: Along the edge from its sharp corner (the first edge from (4.763, -8.25) to (4.763, 8.25)). The slot's cut ends 1.25 mm from each sharp corner, where its inner side would meet the next edge's land; with the 6 in wheel's 5.6 mm run-out at .008 deep, the wheel's centre rocks over 6.81-9.69 mm, and the floor is within 0.1 mm of the STEP's from 2.9 to 13.6 mm along the straight edge; it's held from 3.1 to 13.4, past the groove's inner corners, which neither slot reaches. Beyond, round the noses, the groove rises along the wheel's arc: the exempt nose regions (your decision, 2026-11-06)

speeds.source: The grinder's spindle at 3,450 rpm, a two-pole motor as on SB1029 and Clausing (its station, moonshot/library/stations/sgrind.json spindle rpm), runs the 6 in wheel at 5,420 sfpm, inside Machinery's Handbook's 5,000-6,000 sfpm for diamond wheels. [proposed: the down-feed, .0005 in a pass, 16 passes to .008 and two spark-outs, the light end for resin diamond on carbide]. The stroke is what the slot's ends allow (region)

operations.what: Grind the second edge's chipbreaker: the coolant off and the table run clear, the magnet off, the insert turned 120 deg between its keepers, the magnet and the coolant on again, then ground as the first

region.note: As edge1's, on the second edge

operations.what: Grind the third edge's chipbreaker: the insert turned another 120 deg the same way, then ground as the first
operations.note: Turned as for the second edge: the coolant off and the table run clear, the magnet off, the insert turned, the magnet and the coolant on again

region.note: As edge1's, on the third edge

finish.title: Quick check
finish.what: Check the .125 thickness with the micrometer, the chipbreaker's .010 land and .055 groove on each edge on the comparator, and the groove's .008 depth with the test indicator on the height gauge's stand

proposed.what: The stock: a TPGN 322 C2 insert bought ground, only the chipbreaker ground here
proposed.why: The drawing gives only the finished insert; the shop's routing has one grinding operation, the chipbreaker on the Harig (note 1)

proposed.what: The keepers: three 1/8 x 1/2 x 1-1/2 in keepers cut from precision ground O-1 flat stock, laid flat in a pinwheel, the first flush with the chuck's back edge
proposed.why: Your decision is ground steel keepers; 1/8 in thick they stand at the insert's own .125; cut 1-1/2 in long they fit round it on the chuck in a pinwheel (23 mm behind its middle, 35 in front), which the shop's 6 in parallels don't; the chuck's back edge squares the first to the table's travel within the land's ±.005

proposed.what: The diamond wheel: a 6 x .035 x 1-1/4 in 1A1R resin-bond slotting wheel, 120 grit, on its own hub, on the grinder for the job and its mounting not a step
proposed.why: The shop's wheel (gwheel) is aluminium oxide, for steel; the .055 groove needs a wheel narrower than it, ground in two cross positions; a 6 in wheel's run-out (5.6 mm at .008) leaves more of each edge at full depth than the grinder's 10 in (7.2 mm, which can't reach .008 anywhere on an edge without touching the next land); a carbide shop keeps its diamond wheel on its own hub
The light end for resin diamond on carbide; the spindle's 3,450 rpm is the grinder's station's (sgrind.json), which runs the 6 in wheel at 5,420 sfpm, inside the Handbook's diamond range
